reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999, Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
scope: Additive source extraction only, no change to live galleries, prior species files, licenses, BONAP evidence.

morphology.habit: Annual 10–80(–100) cm, fibrous-rooted tuft, persistent taproot absent
morphology.leaves: Basal and cauline deeply lobed/pinnate; terminal segments suborbicular to obovate, commonly wavy
morphology.heads: Radiate yellow heads; phyllaries ca. 5 mm and ray ligules ca. 4.5 mm
morphology.fruits: Cypselae ca. 1.7 mm with fine hairs, rarely glabrous; genus capillary pappus
morphology.habitat: Moist disturbed, often sandy and partly shaded places

notes: Flora warns basal leaf-lobe attachment does not always reliably distinguish P. glabella from P. tampicana.

records.printed_flora_page: Packera obovata (Muhl. ex Willd.) W.A.Weber & Á.Löve

morphology.habit: Rhizomatous and usually stoloniferous perennial 20–50(–70) cm, fibrous-rooted
morphology.leaves: Basal blades ovate to orbicular, less than 1.5× as long as broad; often purplish beneath; upper leaves reduced
morphology.heads: Yellow radiate heads; phyllaries 3–7 mm, ligules 5–10 mm
morphology.fruits: Cypselae ca. 2.3 mm, usually glabrous; pappus bristles up to 6 mm

notes: Early-season blooming and basal leaf shape are useful; do not substitute flowering season for fruit confirmation.

morphology.habit: Glabrous low taprooted annual 10–40(–80) cm; taproot can be weak and obscured by laterals
morphology.leaves: Deeply lobed basal and stem leaves with subreniform toothed terminal segment, some anthocyanic coloration below
morphology.fruit: Pappus white capillary bristles per genus
morphology.habitat: Low open prairies, roadsides and disturbed sites

notes: 1999 regional key separates from P. glabella by taproot and often slender narrow-based leaf lobes, explicitly warns the lobes aren't wholly reliable.

morphology.leaves: Alternate, linear blades 1–4 mm wide, glandular-based hairs
morphology.heads: Discoid; no ray florets; narrow linear phyllaries 0.6–1.2 mm wide and about 3–5 mm long
morphology.flowers: Tubular pink/purple disk florets, anthers brownish to reddish purple; genus corolla lobes deeply divided
morphology.fruits: Cypselae 3–5 mm, pappus 7–10 scales (genus), scales 0.5–2 mm for key branch

notes: Do not confuse rayless P. callosa with showy-rayed P. reverchonii or P. hookeriana.

morphology.leaves: Lower blades deeply once or twice pinnatifid; upper leaves reduced
morphology.heads: Numerous small heads 3–4 mm wide in open branching array
morphology.rays: Minute white ray limbs under 1 mm, pistillate and fertile
morphology.discs: White, morphologically perfect but functionally staminate/infertile
morphology.fruits: Black cypselae (2–)2.5(–3.5) mm, pappus 2 petaloid scales

notes: Source warns of dermatitis caused by sesquiterpene lactones; no manipulation/field handling advice implied.
Ray fertility is unusual and important for learner anatomy.

records.printed_flora_page: Pectis angustifolia Torr. var. fastigiata (A.Gray) D.J.Keil

morphology.habit: Strongly fragrant, much-branched perennial or occasional annual, fibrous roots and sometimes woody stem base; stems 5–15 cm
morphology.leaves: Linear 10–40 × 1–2 mm, revolute, glabrous except 1–2 mm bristles at basal margins; conspicuously oil gland-punctate
morphology.heads: Clustered near branch tips, peduncles 3–30 mm
morphology.phyllaries: Single series of subequal 2.5–4.5 mm keeled bracts, each with conspicuous subterminal gland 0.5–1 mm and small additional glands
morphology.fruits: Cypselae 2.5–3.5 mm; pappus 0–4 short scales 0.5–1(–2) mm

notes: Variety treatment: do not propagate diagnostic counts to unverified P. angustifolia records.

morphology.leaves: Opposite low on stems, alternate above; blades ovate/lance-ovate 2–5 cm, punctate, essentially glabrous, coarsely serrate/small-lobed; petioles 4–10 mm
morphology.rays: 3–5 short fertile yellow rays; ligules 2.5–3 mm
morphology.fruits: Cypselae 2–2.8 mm, pappus usually a single 0.5–1.8 mm bristle with vestigial scales

notes: Crosswalk from current Laphamia lindheimeri to historical Perityle lindheimeri requires nomenclatural confirmation; source character extraction kept as provisional concept.

morphology.habit: Small perennial 10–30 cm, slender to stout woody branching root
morphology.leaves: Mostly basal, oblong-lanceolate to linear, entire, toothed or lobed
morphology.heads: Single large terminal head 15–25 mm high including corollas, overlapping semi-scarious phyllaries with dark tips
morphology.florets: All ligulate, upper side pale/white and lower side pink to deep lavender-rose, innermost sometimes yellowish
morphology.fruits: Cypsela pappus of abundant capillary bristles (specific fruit body length unreported)

notes: Do not describe central disk florets: heads are entirely ligulate.

morphology.habit: Aromatic herb, annual or perennial, reaching 2 m
morphology.leaves: Alternate, elliptic to oblong elliptic, entire to serrate, petiolate, puberulent below with resin globules on both faces
morphology.heads: Numerous pink/rose-purple disciform heads in elongated panicle, terminal central axis matures before shorter laterals
morphology.phyllaries: Minutes sessile resin globules, inner/middle nearly glabrous except glands, outer sparse hairs
morphology.florets: Peripheral fertile pistillate and central perfect infertile florets; no rays
morphology.fruits: Cylinder cypsela below 1 mm with fine barbellate bristles (genus)

notes: Existing learner describes rounded corymbiform mass; regional key emphasizes elongated panicle and shorter lateral axes.

morphology.leaves: Alternate, ovate, lanceolate or elliptic, entire to serrate, nearly glabrous through tomentose, resin globules sometimes present
morphology.heads: Many rose/purple disciform heads, cymose lateral branches eventually overtake central axis, making flattened/layered flowering arrays
morphology.phyllaries: Outermost and median copiously puberulent and ciliate; inner hairs mainly tips
morphology.florets: Peripheral fertile pistillate, central perfect infertile; ray florets absent
morphology.fruits: Cylindric cypsela under 1 mm, capillary bristle pappus per genus

notes: Regional source distinguishes P. camphorata by involucral pubescence, arrangement of flowering axes; scent shared by both.

morphology.habit: Aromatic annual, upright 0.1–1 m, white-woolly to nearly glabrous
morphology.leaves: Basal oblanceolate/spatulate; stem alternate, narrow 3–10 cm × 2–10 mm, green or sparsely glandular above and white woolly below, not decurrent
morphology.heads: Numerous closely clustered disciform heads, involucres 5–7 mm, phyllaries whitish with rusty tint at maturity
morphology.florets: No rays; all disk-like florets fertile in original genus circumscription
morphology.fruits: Cypselae 0.8–1.2 mm; pappus of bristles dispersed individually/in clusters

notes: Differentiate woolly-both-sides decurrent-leaved P. stramineum from green-above P. obtusifolium.

holds.reason: 1999 regional flora lacks matching species treatment; needs FNA or western flora.
Variety fastigiata documented separately; species-wide account not assumed.
Earlier variety versus historic Iva angustifolia crosswalk remains unresolved.
